reason: Mounting the motor with its clutch seems like a useful first step toward driving the attractions.
expectation: I expect a mounted motor assembly; I am not yet sure how it will drive the two attractions at different speeds.

alternatives.reason: The pulley pair also seems relevant to changing speed, but I chose to prepare the motor first.

effect: The motor and clutch are now assembled and ready to mount.
reaction: A straightforward preparation; its role in the two-speed drive is still unclear.
reason: Mounting the assembly should put the motor in place to drive the attractions.
expectation: I expect the clutched motor to be attached to the whale, with further connections still needed.

alternatives.reason: The pulleys may set the theatre's speed, but mounting the motor first seems practical.

effect: The motor is now mounted on the whale, ready for its drive connections.
reaction: Straightforward progress; I am curious how the two speeds will be arranged.
reason: The flexible coupler should connect the motor to a crank.
expectation: I expect it to connect one attraction to the motor, though I am not sure which one yet.

alternatives.reason: The pulley pair also needs assembly, but I chose to connect the mounted motor first.

effect: The coupler connected the motor to the dragon; the theatre still needs its drive.
reaction: It is useful to see which attraction the coupler serves, though the result gives little mechanical detail.
reason: The pulley pair is the only offered combination and should help drive the theatre.
expectation: I expect an assembled pulley pair that can be fitted to the theatre drive, possibly changing its speed.

effect: The two pulleys are assembled; they still need a belt and connection to the whale.
reaction: Straightforward preparation, with the speed relationship still unexplained.
reason: The belt is the only offered combination and should link the pulleys.
expectation: I expect a belted pulley assembly ready to fit to the theatre drive.

effect: The belt and pulleys form a reducing drive, suggesting the theatre will turn more slowly.
reaction: The name clarifies the speed relationship, although I would like to see how it works.
reason: Fitting the reducing drive is the only offered combination and should connect the theatre to the motor.
expectation: I expect the theatre to be connected through the belt drive so it turns more slowly than the motor.

effect: The fitted belt drive makes the star wheel turn more slowly than the dragon, explaining how the different pulley sizes set their speeds.
reaction: The explanation makes the speed difference satisfying and clear.
reason: The clear cover is the only offered combination and should guard the moving drive.
expectation: I expect the belt and pulleys to be covered while remaining visible.

effect: The fair drive is now guarded, leaving the accessory switch to operate it.
reaction: A sensible safety step, though the result adds little detail.
reason: The switch key is the only offered combination and should let me operate the attractions.
expectation: I expect the motor to run the dragon and star wheel at their different speeds.

effect: The switch runs both attractions, and the clutch provides a gentle slip if the dragon is held still. The chapter's goal is complete.
reaction: Seeing the dragon and stars work together is a satisfying payoff; the clutch detail adds a useful safety insight.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the reducing drive was most worthwhile: the explanation made the different pulley speeds clear and connected them to the dragon and stars.

leastWorthwhile.text: Assembling the pulleys and belt felt somewhat repetitive before their role was explained.

surprise.text: The clutch slipping when the dragon is held still was a useful detail I had not expected.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, although the early motor and pulley preparations offered little explanation until the drive was fitted.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see the lifting test after getting the attractions working, especially because the story distinguishes its invented lift from the real mechanisms.
